messages:
olivia: Quick sync — Nova Labs wants a POC for a chat summarization endpoint. Requirements: sustained 200 qps, microbursts to 2k qps for ~60s, gen len ~128, SLO p99 <= 300ms. Can we do this on Dedicated + hosted fallback? Need cost estimate, runbook, security checklist. When can we run an initial smoke test?

kai: For a profile like this we usually recommend a 2-3 shard Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) with autoscale + hosted fallback. Which model are they planning to use? redwood-1-3b vs. 7b matters. Quantization will change latency — int8 tends to help but we need to validate quality.

maria: Ops question — do they need multi-AZ? If yes, warm standby across regions adds headroom and complexity. Also need the exact burst waveform (single spike vs. sustained waves) to size queues.

alex-pricing: Ballpark numbers to start: Dedicated baseline (~$X/hr per shard) + per-token hosted fallback. If they commit 6mo we can do ~15% off. I can produce a commit vs monthly comparison once we have expected tokens/sec.

olivia: Burst shape: mostly steady 200 qps, but during peaks they fan out 20–30% of users causing ~10% chance of 2k qps spikes for ~45–75s. Nova prefers redwood-1-3b quantized if perf/quality holds.

jordan-eng: Quick tech notes — with adaptive batching + prefix KV cache we can usually hold p99 < 300ms at 200 qps on 2-3 A100-class GPUs for a 3B quantized model. Hitting 2k sustained without adding burst capacity will push us into hosted fallback routing. Canary plan: ramp 50 -> 200 qps over 10m, then run two controlled 60s 2k bursts to validate routing/fallback.

devops-bot: capacity-estimate: dedicated_shards=3, instance_type=A100-80GB-eq, est_peak_tokens_per_sec=14000, expected_workers_per_shard=4

maria: Runbook (short): 1) monitor queue length and token-backlog 2) if queue > 70% capacity, flip fallback-routing to hosted 3) alert: p95 > 200ms or error_rate > 0.5% 4) rollback policy: scale-down to safe qps and toggle canary off. I'll draft a playbook.

natalie-sec: Security checklist: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for customer keys, network diagram for Private vs Dedicated, and confirmation of whether customer PII/PCI will be sent. If they will send PCI data we should recommend Private deployment to limit scope.

olivia: Can someone drop a simple loadtest command we can hand to the customer (non-invasive, reproducible)? Also we need a one-page pricing summary I can share in the next call.

kai: Example (vegeta):
```
echo "POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\"model\":\"redwood-1-3b\",\"input\":\"summarize: ...\",\"max_tokens\":128}" > req.txt
vegeta attack -duration=60s -rate=200 -targets=req.txt | vegeta report
```

alex-pricing: I'll prep the pricing sheet. Olivia — confirm whether Nova wants monthly or annual commit; monthly first usually works. Also will add a column showing hosted fallback unit costs so they can see marginal burn during bursts.

olivia: Monthly first, we can negotiate a 6mo commit if POC shows stable profiles. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: I'll own the runbook and can join the POC kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. Kai/jordan — can you be available for the 60s-burst test?

kai: I can join the burst window.

jordan-eng: I'll be on standby to watch runtimes and fetch KV cache dumps.

olivia: Great — assembling doc and calendar invite now. I'll attach the pricing and the vegeta command to the invite.
